content:
Priya M.: Quick RFC follow-up — local coordinator vs central fallback controller. I sketched tradeoffs and a hybrid we could try for canary/A-B rollouts. TL;DR: local fast decisions for latency-critical paths + central arbitration for consistency and observability.
Alex B.: can you summarize the main failure modes you're trying to cover?
Priya M.: sure — 1) model regressions (quality), 2) sudden capacity loss (runtime OOMs / node failures), 3) regional/network partitions, 4) slow global telemetry causing stale decisions.
Samir K.: nice list. For (4) I worry if local decisions diverge too long — we end up with split-brain where 2 canaries behave differently.
Priya M.: agreed. Hybrid idea: local coordinator has a tiny, deterministic policy engine for immediate fallbacks (latency < 5ms added), plus it emits a compact action log to central controller. Central controller evaluates longer-window signals and can send corrective commands (drain, rollback, pin variant).
Elena R.: that sounds promising. What does the local policy look like? simple thresholds?
Priya M.: yes — local policy is a minimal state machine: if error-rate > X or p95 latency > Y or throughput saturation > Z for N consecutive requests -> local fallback to a compatible variant. It must be conservative: prefer safe model variant or older pinned version.
Marco L.: compatibility matrix concern: local fallback requires each node to know which variants are compatible. How do we keep that list up-to-date without pinging central for every request?
Priya M.: keep a compact compatibility blob distributed via config sync (cached for T minutes). Local checks are purely about metrics, not discovery.
Alex B.: what about private deployments? customers can be air-gapped, so central controller might not exist. Local-first solves that, but then we lose global telemetry/rollouts.
Priya M.: Exactly — hybrid must degrade gracefully: if central unreachable, local operates in autonomous mode and records actions to local durable log. Once connectivity is restored, it ships the log to central for reconciliation.
Samir K.: reconcile is tricky. We need idempotency and ordering. Maybe use monotonically increasing sequence numbers per node and accept out-of-order arrival at central: central will accept actions and recompute the canonical state.
Elena R.: also need rate-limits on local fallback churn to prevent oscillation. e.g., backoff window after a local fallback before it can flip again.
Priya M.: yes: policy includes a cooldown and exponential backoff with jitter.
Alex B.: what telemetry do we need to send to central to make effective decisions without overloading control plane?
Priya M.: minimal action log + rolling aggregates: {"window_summaries": ["p50","p95","error_rate","qps"], "sampled_traces": "1/1000", "action_events": "list of fallback/rollforward/rollback"}
Keep sizes bounded — we can downsample aggressively from edge.
Marco L.: can we get a sample config for the local policy?
Priya M.: putting a short example below:
```json
{
  "policy_version": "1",
  "triggers": {
    "error_rate": {"threshold": 0.03, "consecutive_windows": 3},
    "p95_latency_ms": {"threshold": 350, "consecutive_windows": 2},
    "oom_count": {"threshold": 1}
  },
  "fallback_action": "switch_to_compatible_variant",
  "cooldown_s": 120,
  "backoff_multiplier": 2
}
```
Alex B.: looks reasonable. How do we ensure the local fallback action is reversible once central decides rollback wasn't necessary?
Priya M.: central can issue an "undo" or a new canonical directive with higher precedence. All local actions are stamped with origin=local and a monotonic action id. Central directives include a generation counter for the pinned variant; local respects central precedence when generation higher.
Samir K.: we should also define the semantics for mixed-origin authority. e.g., origin priorities: capacity-safety > central-pin > central-suggestion > local-autonomy.
Elena R.: don't forget about billing/usage and observability: if local flips lots, Cost team needs to know. Include cost-impact field in central aggregates.
Marco L.: operational runbooks? if central and local disagree for > 10 minutes, alert oncall with baked remediation (mute local autonomy or force revert).
Priya M.: yes — propose an automatic escalation path: 10m divergent -> page oncall + optional auto-enforce (config flag per deployment).
Alex B.: latency risk: local checks add CPU. Keep them tiny. Prefer sampling and use existing runtime stats rather than new instrumentation.
Samir K.: also consider a debug-mode to capture full traces for short windows when investigating rollouts. Not default.
Priya M.: open questions I want feedback on: 1) action-log schema (compact vs verbose), 2) reconciliation algorithm (accept last-write-wins with seq nums vs CRDT-like merge), 3) default thresholds and cooldowns for general workloads.
Elena R.: my vote: compact action-log + LWW with seq numbers and central re-eval for conflicts. Simpler to implement and auditable.
Marco L.: agree on LWW. For private deployments, expose a local-only mode switch in config so central isn't expected.
Alex B.: I'll prototype a small control-plane API for directives: POST /v1/directives {target, generation, action, reason}. simple auth token for now.
Priya M.: thanks Alex. Samir, can you take on reconciliation design? maybe draft a short RFC section describing seq num authority and safety checks.
Samir K.: sure, will do. Target a short RFC blurb by EOD Friday.
deploy-bot: "deployment: canary-proto 0.1.3 -> staging succeeded" :white_check_mark:
Priya M.: thanks all. I'll update the RFC with the hybrid flow, include the policy snippet and a proposed runbook. tagging @Alex B., @Samir K., @Elena R. for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Alex B.: ack. couple follow-ups: add a note about metric cardinality and memory budget for local aggregator.
Elena R.: and add example alerts for divergence.
Marco L.: add compatibility with VPC/private mode as a parameter.
Samir K.: I'll include edge cases: replay storms during reconnect, and ordering gaps.
Priya M.: great — I'll PR the RFC update tomorrow morning and ping this thread.
